LESSON: READING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Reading 2.7Reading Aloud (Articulation) (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub-strand
Topic 2.8: Reading Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading Comprehension, part of Reading 2.7Reading Aloud (Articulation) (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub-strand in Grade 8 GERMAN.

Key inquiry question: How do we ensure we get all the required information from a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify specific words for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read texts for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the role of vocabulary in comprehension.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify specific words for comprehension,

   Reading Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read texts for comprehension,

   Reading Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the role of vocabulary in comprehension.

   Reading Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read short simple texts on physical features and identify them with peers

2. read texts on activities people do in varying weather conditions and match to given pictures,

3. read online texts on physical features in Kenya and Germany and share findings with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read short simple texts on physical features and identify them with peers
2. read texts on activities people do in varying weather conditions and match to given pictures,
3. read online texts on physical features in Kenya and Germany and share findings with peers.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: The learner develops skills of interacting with technology when they read online texts on physical features in

Kenya and Germany and share findings with peers.

Patriotism: The learner develops an appreciation of their country as they read online texts on physical features in Kenya and share

findings with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:

Environmental awareness: The learner develops environmental awareness when they read short simple texts on activities people

do in varying weather conditions.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner relates the topic of talking about the weather and environment to the same concepts in Social Studies.
